source_snapshot.procedure: Follow Intel Server System Validation Manual Guide.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: An operator uses unspecified Intel SSV margin tooling and compares unspecified LTSSM behavior with an unavailable manual/specification.

original_test_intent.purpose: Undetermined beyond a broad Intel PCIe validation context: the row may intend electrical/receiver lane-margin measurement, LTSSM transition/steady-state behavior validation, or a prescribed SSV flow combining them.
original_test_intent.target: An unidentified Intel server PCIe root-port/endpoint/link set; the source supplies no root complex, endpoint, BDF, link generation/width, retimer/switch path or platform SKU.
original_test_intent.scope: Cannot be fixed safely because `PCIe Link Margin` and `LTSSM` name distinct technical observations and the only procedure/criterion defer to missing documents.
original_test_intent.operation: No executable or manual operation can be selected until the owner identifies the intended SSV test, manual revision, hardware/tool path, stimuli and affected links.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: Workbook timing is 60 attended and 720 machine minutes, but no iteration, dwell, margin sweep, retrain count or LTSSM capture window is defined.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Undefined; `behavior follows the specification` supplies no state sequence, L0/recovery rule, margin metric, threshold, error limit or comparison reference.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: At minimum, the owner must provide the intended test type and manual section, platform/link map, qualified tool/version, exact stimulus/sweep/capture, numeric/state acceptance criteria, raw output, PCIe/AER/device health, restoration and recovery evidence.
ambiguities: The row does not say whether LTSSM observation, lane-margin measurement, or a combined Intel SSV workflow is requested.
No manual title/revision/section, tool, topology, target, command, stimulus, threshold, duration semantics or recovery exists.
The public Intel Link Inspector and Lane Margin Tool demonstrate different evidence types; neither can be chosen as the missing SSV procedure by inference.
source_conflicts: Test Set says PCIe Link Margin while Items says LTSSM, and the missing delegated procedure provides no way to determine whether those are intended as one flow or two different tests.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly refuses to guess an Intel procedure or threshold and keeps the case blocked. Its reason reads mainly as missing documentation/tooling, which alone would normally be a provisionable readiness issue; it does not identify the deeper semantic fork between lane-margin measurement and LTSSM state-transition validation.

applicable_history.decision: A missing SOP alone is not BLOCKED, but BLOCKED remains correct when purpose/operation/acceptance cannot be deterministically identified and plausible interpretations require materially different stimuli and evidence.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: BLOCKED is retained for a genuine semantic reason, not merely because a package is absent. Lane-margin measurement and LTSSM transition validation are different activities with different tools, stimuli and acceptance evidence; the row does not identify which one the Intel SSV manual intended.

available_now: Only the broad Intel server PCIe validation domain and the two labels `PCIe Link Margin` and `LTSSM` are known.
Safe read-only PCIe topology, current link state/capability, firmware and baseline AER/kernel/BMC evidence can be collected, but such inventory cannot complete or disambiguate the requested test.
missing_inputs: Authoritative owner statement selecting lane margin, LTSSM state behavior, or a named combined SSV testcase
Intel Server System Validation Manual exact title/revision/section and platform/SKU applicability
Qualified tool/package/fixture/version/license, root-port/endpoint/BDF/link/retimer topology and supported link generation/width
Exact stimulus/sweep/retrain/capture sequence, 720-minute meaning, acceptance thresholds/states/error limits, side effects, approval, restoration and recovery
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The Intel platform/PCIe validation owner must disambiguate intent and supply the matching proprietary reference/tool; the lab/device owners then define safe targets, fixture, limits, maintenance and recovery.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Inventory PCIe root ports, bridges, switches/retimers and endpoints by BDF; record LnkCap/LnkSta, AER capability/counters, firmware/BIOS and attached-device identities without retraining or clearing logs
Record active workloads, baseline kernel/BMC/SEL/device health, OOB recovery availability and candidate package metadata without installing or executing it
prohibited_until_closed: Do not choose Intel Lane Margin Tool, FPGA Link Inspector, lspci retrain, compliance patterns or any SSV command by guess; do not manipulate link speed/width/equalization/LTSSM/registers
Do not call inventory or L0 presence a margin result, apply FPGA-specific public documentation to a server root complex, clear evidence, or issue PASS/FAIL while purpose and criteria remain undefined
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The owner provides a signed intent statement and exact manual section whose procedure, target, evidence and acceptance form one deterministic test; tool/platform compatibility and side effects are reviewed, and a bounded recovery plan is approved before reclassification for execution.

revision_candidate.test_name: PCIe LTSSM or Link-Margin Validation — Owner Clarification Required
revision_candidate.purpose: BLOCKED: determine whether the testcase is an LTSSM state-transition validation, a PCIe lane-margin measurement, or a specifically named Intel SSV combined flow before defining any execution contract.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Unknown Intel server platform and PCIe path; exact CPU/PCH/root complex, board/BIOS, endpoint, switch/retimer, generation/width, tool and manual applicability must be supplied.
revision_candidate.target_scope: No mutable target is authorized. Read-only inventory may cover candidate PCIe paths solely to support owner clarification.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Selected technical intent; Intel manual title/revision/section; exact platform/link topology; qualified tool/fixture/version/license; stimuli/sweep/capture and 720-minute semantics; measurable state or margin limits; logs; side effects; approval; restoration and recovery.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Do not generate a test command. After clarification, transcribe and review the matching owner-approved flow without substituting a different public Intel tool or treating LTSSM state observation as lane-margin measurement.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Purpose and acceptance are unambiguous, source conflict is resolved, manual/tool/platform compatibility is verified, affected devices are idle and recoverable, baselines preserved, side effects and abort limits known, and change approval/OOB recovery available.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Owner clarification and reference provenance; exact target map; tool/config/command; raw LTSSM sequence or voltage/time margin data as applicable; numeric/state comparison; PCIe/AER/kernel/BMC/device deltas; timing; restoration and final device/link health.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact owner-selected Intel SSV manual section and platform specification. No generic `follow specification` or public tool example is sufficient.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Read-only inventory only while blocked. No link retrain, margin sweep, compliance state, register write, speed/width change, reset, unreviewed tool or inferred threshold.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Owner clarification and explicit approval are mandatory before any state-changing action; qualified PCIe/lab personnel must approve fixture, target and recovery.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Unknown until the actual procedure is supplied. Do not assume that missing tooling makes the final flow manual or automated.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No recovery action is authorized while blocked. The clarified flow must include restoration of link/device state, preserved evidence, OOB access and device/host recovery before execution classification is revisited.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Any unresolved purpose/target/criterion, missing manual applicability, tool mismatch, uncertain side effect, active workload, absent OOB recovery, or attempt to substitute a different LTSSM/margin method.

identified_defects: The Test Set and Item can denote two materially different PCIe validation activities.
The procedure and criterion are complete external-reference placeholders with no revision or section.
No target, operation, duration semantics, observable metric or acceptance value exists.
V2's blocked rationale does not distinguish this genuine semantic ambiguity from an ordinary missing vendor package/SOP.
reason_for_change: Retain BLOCKED on the correct V3 basis: the testcase cannot yet be defined, and choosing among plausible LTSSM and lane-margin interpretations would invent the test rather than merely provision a missing tool.

new_technical_evidence.title: Intel PCI Express Lane Margin Tool
new_technical_evidence.supports: Lane margin tooling obtains voltage and time margin information for capable PCIe receivers.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The source does not say that this public tool or receiver-margin procedure is the intended Intel SSV flow.

new_technical_evidence.title: Intel PCIe Link Inspector
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Intel FPGA debug toolkit only, not automatically an Intel server SSV path
new_technical_evidence.supports: LTSSM inspection records state transitions and can dump a sequence, which is a distinct output from voltage/time lane-margin measurement.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: This FPGA-specific workflow must not be applied to the unidentified server platform.

removed_ambiguities: Explains exactly why the row remains semantically blocked rather than treating a missing manual as the only problem.
Separates safe topology inventory from both candidate state-changing validation flows.
Defines the evidence required to close the ambiguity without selecting a tool by model inference.
remaining_blockers: Purpose, target, operation, acceptance, tool/manual applicability and recovery are all unresolved; BLOCKED remains necessary until the owner selects and documents one deterministic flow.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 preserves V2's safe BLOCKED result but supplies the specific technical proof required by the new logic: public Intel materials show that LTSSM sequence observation and voltage/time lane-margin measurement are distinct, so the source labels cannot be merged by assumption. This avoids both over-BLOCKING for a mere missing package and unsafe reclassification of a genuinely undefined test.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The Test Set says PCIe Link Margin, the Item says LTSSM, and both Procedure and Criteria defer to unspecified Intel references.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 blocks for missing manual/tool/criteria; V3 proves the deeper lane-margin-versus-LTSSM semantic fork and lists safe inventory that may proceed.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: No link-changing command or substitute tool while blocked; only read-only topology/link/AER baselines may be collected for owner clarification.
